## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API

| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` | Streaming or non-streaming chat |

## 3.2 Chat request

```json
{
  "model": "qwen",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "stream": false
}
```

`model` is an alias, or `"auto"` to use priority order. `messages` is required.
Unsupported OpenAI request fields are ignored because provider web UIs do not expose
their corresponding controls.

Successful responses use OpenAI-compatible JSON or SSE and include `X-Provider`.
`X-Conversation-Id` identifies the retained browser tab; send it in a later request to
continue that tab. Non-streaming requests collect the provider output before writing
JSON. Streaming requests wait for the first output token before committing SSE headers,
so a zero-token provider failure can still fall back.

`GET /v1/models` keeps the standard OpenAI list shape. Its entries combine configured
aliases with model or bot labels last discovered from each authenticated provider page.
The `owned_by` field identifies the provider. Discovery runs outside request handling,
at most once per 24 hours, and keeps the last successful result when a page cannot be
read. Model IDs remain the provider's visible label when unique. If two providers expose
the same label, both remain available under collision-safe IDs such as
`qwen:Shared-Model` and `metaai:Shared-Model`; the proxy translates the selected ID back to
the provider's visible label before browser interaction. An existing configured alias
keeps its unqualified ID; only the colliding provider entries are qualified.

## 3.3 Routing and errors

The selected alias is attempted first, followed by enabled providers in priority order.
Degraded providers are skipped. An immediate adapter error or a response channel that
closes with zero output marks the provider degraded and permits fallback before response
bytes are committed. Once SSE output has started, transparent fallback is no longer safe;
a later provider failure can only end that stream.

The dashboard request log records the attempted providers, fallback state, actual
provider, model, status, and duration. `max_tokens` and `temperature` are accepted for
OpenAI compatibility but are not forwarded because the current web adapters do not have
equivalent controls. Invalid requests return HTTP 400; no configured or available
provider returns HTTP 503.

The detailed handler, routing, browser, and output sequence is specified in
[Chapter 12](./12-performance.md).# Chapter 3 — OpenAI-Compatible API
